claim: 82.3 ± 3.8% of all RGLs were positive for GFP in the hippocampus of P70 Ascl1KIGFP mice and therefore transcribed Ascl1.
source: We found that 82.3 ± 3.8% of all RGLs were positive for GFP in the hippocampus of P70 Ascl1KIGFP mice and therefore transcribed Ascl1.
evidence: Quantitative data from immunolabeling experiments in Ascl1KIGFP reporter mice showing percentage of GFP+ RGLs

claim: Only 1.9 ± 0.3% of RGLs expressed Ascl1 protein at a level detected with anti-Ascl1 antibodies.
source: In contrast, only 1.9 ± 0.3% of these cells expressed Ascl1 protein at a level detected with anti-Ascl1 antibodies (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Quantitative immunolabeling data shown in Figure 1A and B

claim: 83.8 ± 4.1% of the RGLs that did not express Ki67 and were therefore quiescent expressed GFP, indicating a transcriptionally active Ascl1 locus.
source: Notably, 83.8 ± 4.1% of the RGLs that did not express Ki67 and were therefore quiescent expressed GFP, indicating a transcriptionally active Ascl1 locus (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: Quantitative data from co-immunolabeling for GFP and Ki67 in RGLs shown in Figure 1C and D

claim: GFP immunolabeling intensity was comparable in active Ki67+ RGLs and quiescent Ki67- RGLs.
source: Moreover, GFP immunolabeling intensity was comparable in active Ki67+ RGLs and quiescent Ki67- RGLs (Figure 1E).
evidence: Quantitative comparison of GFP intensity levels shown in Figure 1E

claim: Ascl1 transcripts are present at similar levels in quiescent and active RGLs as confirmed by single molecule in situ hybridization.
source: We confirmed the presence of Ascl1 transcripts at similar levels in quiescent and active RGLs using single molecule in situ hybridization (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: Single molecule RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1F,G

claim: Ascl1 protein expression in quiescent hippocampal RGLs is regulated by a non-transcriptional mechanism.
source: The finding that quiescent and proliferating RGLs transcribe the Ascl1 gene at comparable levels but only proliferating RGLs express detectable levels of Ascl1 protein, indicates that Ascl1 protein expression in quiescent hippocampal RGLs is regulated by a non-transcriptional mechanism.
evidence: Inference based on the observation that Ascl1 mRNA is present but protein is absent in quiescent RGLs

claim: BMP4 induces NSCs to stop proliferating and enter a reversible quiescent state.
source: Similarly, we found that NSCs originating from the adult hippocampus and maintained in culture in the presence of FGF2 stopped proliferating and entered a reversible quiescent state when exposed to BMP4 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: Experimental data from NSC cultures showing cell cycle arrest upon BMP4 treatment, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D

claim: 1839 genes were differentially expressed between NSCs in proliferating and quiescent states.
source: RNA sequencing analysis revealed that 1839 genes were differentially expressed between NSCs in proliferating and quiescent states (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F

claim: Ascl1 RNA levels were not significantly different between proliferating and quiescent NSC conditions.
source: Ascl1 RNA levels were not significantly different between these two conditions as verified by QPCR (Figure 2A).
evidence: QPCR data shown in Figure 2A

claim: The intensity of GFP in cultured hippocampal NSCs derived from Ascl1KIGFP mice was comparable in proliferating and quiescent conditions.
source: The intensity of GFP in cultured hippocampal NSCs derived from Ascl1KIGFP mice was also comparable in proliferating and quiescent conditions (Figure 2B,C), as for GFP expression in the hippocampus of Ascl1KIGFP mice (Figure 1E).
evidence: Quantitative GFP intensity measurements shown in Figure 2B,C

claim: Ascl1 protein levels were strongly reduced in BMP-treated quiescent NSCs.
source: In contrast, Ascl1 protein levels were strongly reduced in BMP-treated quiescent NSCs (Figure 2D–F), resembling the absence of Ascl1 protein in quiescent hippocampal RGLs in vivo (Figure 1B).
evidence: Immunofluorescence and Western blot data shown in Figure 2D–F

claim: Treatment of quiescent NSCs with proteasome inhibitors significantly increased the levels of Ascl1 protein.
source: Treatment of quiescent NSCs with proteasome inhibitors significantly increased the levels of Ascl1 protein, suggesting that Ascl1 mRNA is translated in quiescent NSCs but Ascl1 protein is rapidly degraded in a proteasome-dependent manner (Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Western blot data after MG132 treatment shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G

claim: Ascl1 protein was similarly reduced in Huwe1 mutant and control NSC cultures upon addition of BMP4.
source: We found that Ascl1 protein was similarly reduced in Huwe1 mutant and control NSC cultures upon addition of BMP4 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H,I), demonstrating that a Huwe1-independent mechanism prompts the down-regulation of Ascl1 protein in quiescent cultured NSCs.
evidence: Immunofluorescence data from Huwe1 mutant NSCs shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H,I

claim: The four Id genes Id1-4 were strongly induced in quiescent NSC cultures.
source: The four Id genes Id1-4 were strongly induced in quiescent NSC cultures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: RNA-Seq data showing Id gene expression changes shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A

claim: Only Id1 and Id4 were clearly upregulated at the protein level upon addition of BMP.
source: Although the transcripts for the four Id genes were induced by BMP4 in NSC cultures (Figure 3A), Id2 and Id3 were already expressed at high levels in proliferating conditions and only Id1 and Id4 were clearly upregulated at the protein level upon addition of BMP (Figure 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Western blot and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C

claim: Id4 expression was highly variable and was absent from cells presenting high levels of Ascl1.
source: Of those, Id4 expression was highly variable and was absent from cells presenting high levels of Ascl1, suggesting a possible negative regulatory relationship between the two proteins, while Id1 was also expressed at various levels but did not anti-correlate with Ascl1 expression levels (Figure 3C–F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–I).
evidence: Immunofluorescence correlation data shown in Figure 3C–F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–I

claim: E47 interacts with Ascl1 in proliferating conditions but with Id4 in quiescence conditions.
source: Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) experiments in NSCs showed that the E protein E47 (a product of the Tcf3/E2A gene) interacts with Ascl1 in proliferating conditions but with Id4 in quiescence conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1J

claim: The interaction between Ascl1 and E47 is disrupted by the presence of Id4.
source: We therefore also carried an in vitro competition-binding assay with separately transfected E47, Ascl1 and Id4 gene products (Figure 3G), which confirmed that the interaction between Ascl1 and E47 is disrupted by the presence of Id4, whilst no interaction was detected between Id4 and Ascl1 (Figure 3H).
evidence: In vitro competition-binding assay data shown in Figure 3G and 3H

claim: The half-life of Ascl1 was reduced from 194 min in proliferating cells to 31 min in quiescent cells.
source: In agreement with monomeric Ascl1 being more unstable than the heterodimer with E47, we found that the half-life of Ascl1 was reduced from 194 min in proliferating cells to 31 min in quiescent cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1K,L).
evidence: Cycloheximide chase experiment data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1K,L

claim: Id4 is expressed in the majority of RGLs (89.6 ± 2.3%).
source: In contrast, Id4 is expressed by the vast majority of RGLs (89.6 ± 2.3%), at high levels in quiescent hippocampal RGLs and at much lower levels in proliferating RGLs (Figure 3I–K), and co-localizes with Ascl1 mRNA-expressing cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2H,I).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 3I–K

claim: Id4 is expressed at high levels in quiescent (Ki67-) RGLs and at much lower levels in proliferating (Ki67+) RGLs.
source: In contrast, Id4 is expressed by the vast majority of RGLs (89.6 ± 2.3%), at high levels in quiescent hippocampal RGLs and at much lower levels in proliferating RGLs (Figure 3I–K), and co-localizes with Ascl1 mRNA-expressing cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2H,I).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 3I–K

claim: Id1 is expressed by 47.5 ± 7.3% of RGLs and is enriched in proliferating cells.
source: Id1 is expressed by a substantial fraction of RGLs (47.5 ± 7.3%) and is enriched in proliferating cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C

claim: Id3 is expressed by 16.9 ± 1.9% of mostly quiescent RGLs, at similar levels in proliferating and quiescent RGLs.
source: Id3 is expressed by a small fraction of mostly quiescent RGLs (16.9 ± 1.9%), at similar levels in proliferating and quiescent RGLs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–G).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–G

claim: Id2 is enriched in granule neurons but not detected in the SGZ.
source: Id1, Id3 and Id4 proteins are clearly expressed in the SGZ of the DG where hippocampal stem cells are located, while Id2 is enriched in granule neurons but not detected in the SGZ (Figure 3I and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–F).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3I and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–F

claim: Id4-transfected NSCs maintained Ascl1 mRNA at levels similar to those of control NSCs but showed markedly reduced Ascl1 protein levels.
source: Id4-transfected NSCs maintained Ascl1 mRNA at levels similar to those of control NSCs but showed markedly reduced Ascl1 protein levels (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: QPCR and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C–E

claim: Transfection of Id4 resulted in a significant decrease in NSC proliferation.
source: Moreover, transfection of Id4 resulted in a significant decrease in NSC proliferation (Figure 4F–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Ki67 and EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 4F–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B

claim: The decrease in proliferation after Id4 transfection was not due to differentiation, since Id4-expressing cells retained expression of the stem cell markers Sox2 and Nestin.
source: This decrease was not due to differentiation, since Id4-expressing cells retained expression of the stem cell markers Sox2 and Nestin (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data for Sox2 and Nestin shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D

claim: Over-expressing Id1, Id2 or Id3 also suppressed Ascl1 protein levels, although Id4 overexpression was most effective.
source: Over-expressing Id1, Id2 or Id3 also suppressed Ascl1 protein levels, although Id4 overexpression was most effective (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data comparing effects of Id1-4 overexpression shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E

claim: Knockdown of Id1-4 in quiescent NSCs by transfection of siRNAs did not significantly affect Ascl1 protein levels.
source: Knockdown of Id1-4 in quiescent NSCs by transfection of siRNAs targeting each Id gene separately or by co-transfection of Id4-siRNA with either Id1-, Id2- or Id3-siRNA, did not significantly affect Ascl1 protein levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F) despite a significant knockdown of each gene at both mRNA and protein levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G–H).
evidence: siRNA knockdown data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F-H

claim: Id4 knockdown resulted in an increase in the protein levels of Id1 and Id3 without affecting their mRNA expression.
source: It is worth noting that Id4 knockdown resulted in an increase in the protein levels of Id1 and Id3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G) without affecting their mRNA expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H), suggesting that Id4 may suppress Id1 and Id3 protein expression.
evidence: Immunofluorescence and QPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G-H

claim: Overexpression of E47 in BMP-treated NSCs resulted in an increase in the levels of Ascl1 protein without significantly affecting Ascl1 mRNA levels.
source: Indeed, overexpression of E47 in BMP-treated NSCs resulted in an increase in the levels of Ascl1 protein without significantly affecting Ascl1 mRNA levels (Figure 4J–L).
evidence: Immunofluorescence and QPCR data shown in Figure 4J–L

claim: Overexpression of E47 was sufficient to partially revert the cell cycle arrest of BMP-treated NSCs.
source: Overexpression of E47 was also sufficient to partially revert the cell cycle arrest of BMP-treated NSCs, and we observed a strong correlation between Ascl1 protein levels and the proliferative state of the cells (Figure 4M,N and Figure 4—figure supplement 1I,J).
evidence: Ki67 and EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 4M,N and Figure 4—figure supplement 1I,J

claim: Expression of Id4 resulted in the up-regulation of 806 genes and down-regulation of 823 genes.
source: Expression of Id4 resulted in the up-regulation of 806 genes and down-regulation of 823 genes (Figure 5A).
evidence: RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 5A

claim: Id4-regulated genes represented 44.2% of the genes regulated by BMP4 in NSCs, including 31.1% of the upregulated and 56.2% of the downregulated genes.
source: Id4-regulated genes represented 44.2% of the genes regulated by BMP4 in NSCs, including 31.1% of the upregulated and 56.2% of the downregulated genes, indicating that Id4 has an important role in the induction of the gene expression program of quiescence downstream of BMP4 (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: RNA-Seq comparison data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–D

claim: Direct transcriptional targets of Ascl1 were strongly downregulated in Id4-overexpressing NSCs, including genes with important roles in cell cycle progression such as Skp2, Cdk1, Cdk2 and Foxm1, as well as other canonical Ascl1 targets such as Dll1 and Dll3.
source: Direct transcriptional targets of Ascl1 were strongly downregulated in Id4-overexpressing NSCs, including genes with important roles in cell cycle progression such as Skp2, Cdk1, Cdk2 and Foxm1, as well as other canonical Ascl1 targets such as Dll1 and Dll3 (Castro et al., 2011; Martynoga et al., 2013) (Figure 5E).
evidence: RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 5E, with citation to previous studies identifying these as Ascl1 targets

claim: The fraction of RGLs expressing Ascl1 increased from 4.4 ± 0.5 in control mice to 15.3 ± 2.7 in Id4cKO mice.
source: The fraction of RGLs expressing Ascl1 increased from 4.4 ± 0.5 in control mice to 15.3 ± 2.7 in Id4cKO mice, with heterozygote mice showing only a small and non-significant increase in the fraction of Ascl1+ RGLs (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6B,C

claim: Ascl1 protein levels were upregulated in Ascl1-expressing RGLs from Id4cKO mice while mRNA levels were lower in RGLs from Id4cKO mice than in control mice.
source: Ascl1 protein levels were also upregulated in Ascl1-expressing RGLs from Id4cKO mice while mRNA levels, measured by single molecule in situ hybridization, were lower in RGLs from Id4cKO mice than in control mice (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Immunofluorescence and RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C

claim: The fraction of proliferating RGLs increased from 4.1 ± 0.5 in control mice to 13.7 ± 2.0 in Id4cKO mice.
source: The fraction of proliferating RGLs increased from 4.1 ± 0.5 in control mice to 13.7 ± 2.0 in Id4cKO mice, while heterozygote mice were indistinguishable from control mice (Figure 6F,G).
evidence: Ki67 immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6F,G

claim: Ascl1 expression was strongly correlated with Ki67 expression in RGLs in control and, particularly, in Id4cKO mice.
source: Ascl1 expression was strongly correlated with Ki67 expression in RGLs in control and, particularly, in Id4cKO mice, supporting the direct link between Ascl1 upregulation and RGL activation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D–F and Andersen et al., 2014; Urbán et al., 2016).
evidence: Co-expression analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D–F, with citations to previous studies

claim: When Id4cKO mice were analyzed 30 days after tamoxifen administration and Id4 deletion, the rate of proliferation of RGLs remained significantly higher than in control mice, although the difference was smaller (3-fold at 5 days and two-fold at 30 days).
source: When Id4cKO mice were analyzed 30 days after tamoxifen administration and Id4 deletion, the rate of proliferation of RGLs remained significantly higher than in control mice, although the difference was smaller (3-fold at 5 days and two-fold at 30 days; Figure 6H).
evidence: Quantification data shown in Figure 6H

claim: There was no difference in the total number of RGLs between Id4cKO and control mice 30 days after Id4 deletion.
source: Since RGL activation is linked to the depletion of the RGL pool (Encinas et al., 2011; Pilz et al., 2018), we quantified the total number of RGLs in Id4cKO and control mice 30 days after Id4 deletion and found no difference between genotypes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: RGL density quantification data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G, with citations to previous studies

claim: Id1 and particularly Id3 were strongly upregulated in RGLs in Id4cKO mice at both 5 days and 30 days after Id4 deletion.
source: To determine whether deletion of Id4 might trigger compensatory mechanisms, we examined the expression of the other Id proteins in Id4cKO mice and found that Id1 and particularly Id3 were strongly upregulated in RGLs in these mice at both 5 days and 30 days after Id4 deletion (Figure 6I–L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 6I–L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H,I

claim: The vast majority of Id3+Ascl1+ cells also express Id4.
source: We found that the majority of Id3+GFAP+ RGLs co-express Ascl1 mRNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 1J,L) and of the Id3+Ascl1+ cells, the vast majority also express Id4 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1K,M).
evidence: RNA in situ hybridization and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1J-M

claim: The function of Id4 in maintenance of RGL quiescence is in remarkable contrast with its role in promoting the proliferation of progenitor cells in the embryonic cerebral cortex.
source: In this study, we show that the repressor protein Id4 promotes the maintenance of adult hippocampal stem cells (RGLs) in a quiescent state. The function of Id4 in maintenance of RGL quiescence is in remarkable contrast with its role in promoting the proliferation of progenitor cells in the embryonic cerebral cortex (Bedford et al., 2005; Yun et al., 2004).
evidence: Comparison with previous studies cited (Bedford et al., 2005; Yun et al., 2004)

claim: In the embryonic forebrain, NSCs are in a proliferative state and proneural bHLH proteins mostly act to promote neuronal differentiation.
source: In the embryonic forebrain, NSCs are in a proliferative state and proneural bHLH proteins mostly act to promote neuronal differentiation.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge of embryonic neural development

claim: Inactivation of proneural bHLH proteins by Id4 during development results in a block of differentiation and extended proliferation.
source: Their inactivation by Id4 during development therefore results in a block of differentiation and extended proliferation.
evidence: Inference based on the role of proneural bHLH proteins in differentiation

claim: In the adult hippocampus, RGLs are mostly quiescent and Ascl1 is required to promote their activity.
source: In contrast, RGLs in the adult hippocampus are mostly quiescent, Ascl1 is required to promote their activity, and inactivation of Ascl1 by Id4 results in their failure to proliferate.
evidence: Statement based on findings from this study and previous knowledge

claim: Inactivation of Ascl1 by Id4 results in RGL failure to proliferate.
source: In contrast, RGLs in the adult hippocampus are mostly quiescent, Ascl1 is required to promote their activity, and inactivation of Ascl1 by Id4 results in their failure to proliferate.
evidence: Inference based on the experimental findings showing Id4 suppresses Ascl1 and maintains quiescence

claim: Id4 promotes the degradation of the pro-activation factor Ascl1 in RGLs.
source: We also show that Id4 promotes the degradation of the pro-activation factor Ascl1 in RGLs.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from the study

claim: Single cell transcriptomic analysis of hippocampal cells did not identify Ascl1 among the genes differentially expressed between quiescent and active stem cells.
source: This surprising finding could be the reason why single cell transcriptomic analysis of hippocampal cells did not identify Ascl1 among the genes differentially expressed between quiescent and active stem cells (Artegiani et al., 2017; Hochgerner et al., 2018; Shin et al., 2015).
evidence: Inference based on the finding that Ascl1 mRNA is present in both quiescent and active cells, with citations to previous studies

claim: Non-transcriptional control of a key activation factor is found in satellite stem cells where the bHLH factor MyoD is transcribed in quiescent cells but its translation is inhibited by an RNA-binding protein to prevent stem cell activation.
source: This non-transcriptional control of a key activation factor is also found, for instance, in satellite stem cells where the bHLH factor MyoD is transcribed in quiescent cells but its translation is inhibited by an RNA-binding protein to prevent stem cell activation (de Morrée et al., 2017).
evidence: Comparison with another stem cell system, citing de Morrée et al., 2017

claim: Id proteins form non-functional heterodimers with E proteins, which are dimerization partners of tissue-specific bHLH transcription factors such as Ascl1.
source: It is well established that Id proteins, including Id4, form non-functional heterodimers with E proteins, which are dimerization partners of tissue-specific bHLH transcription factors such as Ascl1 (Imayoshi and Kageyama, 2014; Ling et al., 2014; Patel et al., 2015; Sharma et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement of established knowledge with multiple citations

claim: The three genes encoding for E proteins in mice are all expressed by RGLs.
source: The three genes encoding for E proteins in mice are all expressed by RGLs, and since they are thought to have redundant functions, it is difficult to investigate their specific contributions to RGL behaviour.
evidence: Statement based on expression data and established knowledge

claim: High levels of Ids result in the sequestration of all E proteins away from functional dimers with Ascl1.
source: Nevertheless, high levels of Ids are expected to result in the sequestration of all E proteins away from functional dimers with Ascl1.
evidence: Inference based on the known mechanism of Id protein action

claim: Non-dimerized Ascl1 is not able to bind DNA.
source: Non-dimerized Ascl1 is not able to bind DNA, and this alone could explain why Ascl1 target genes are downregulated in NSCs upon Id4 overexpression or BMP treatment, which increases the expression of all Id proteins.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge of bHLH protein function

claim: Exposure of different cell types to BMPs triggers the proteolytic degradation of Ascl1.
source: Exposure of different cell types to BMPs has been shown to trigger the proteolytic degradation of Ascl1 (Shou et al., 1999; Viñals et al., 2004).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies (Shou et al., 1999; Viñals et al., 2004)

claim: In lung carcinoma cells, the formation of heterodimers with E47 stabilizes Ascl1, and induction of Id1 by BMP2 sequesters E47, resulting in degradation of the unstable monomeric form of Ascl1.
source: In lung carcinoma cells, the formation of heterodimers with E47 stabilizes Ascl1, and induction of Id1 by BMP2 sequesters E47, resulting in degradation of the unstable monomeric form of Ascl1 (Viñals et al., 2004).
evidence: Statement citing Viñals et al., 2004

claim: Ascl1 is more unstable in quiescent than proliferating hippocampal NSCs.
source: We show that Ascl1 is more unstable in quiescent than proliferating hippocampal NSCs and that Ascl1-E47 dimers are disrupted by Id4.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from the study

claim: Ascl1-E47 dimers are disrupted by Id4.
source: We show that Ascl1 is more unstable in quiescent than proliferating hippocampal NSCs and that Ascl1-E47 dimers are disrupted by Id4.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from the study

claim: E47 overexpression is sufficient to stabilize Ascl1 protein and promote cell cycle re-entry of BMP-treated NSCs.
source: We found that this is indeed sufficient to stabilize Ascl1 protein and promote cell cycle re-entry of BMP-treated NSCs.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from E47 overexpression experiments

claim: Loss of Id4 in hippocampal RGLs resulted in increased Id1 and Id3 protein levels, suggesting that Id4 may suppress these proteins in vivo.
source: Loss of Id4 in hippocampal RGLs also resulted in increased Id1 and Id3 protein levels, suggesting that Id4 may suppress these proteins in vivo, and that its loss may be partially compensated by the increase in their expression.
evidence: Experimental observation from Id4cKO mice with inference about mechanism

claim: Id4 alone contributes to a large extent to the gene expression program induced by BMP to promote NSC quiescence.
source: Our transcriptomic analysis suggests that Id4 alone contributes to a large extent to the gene expression program induced by BMP to promote NSC quiescence.
evidence: Inference based on RNA-Seq analysis comparing Id4 and BMP4 effects

claim: Overexpression of Id4 in the absence of BMP induces many of the genes that BMP4 induces, and suppresses many of the genes suppressed by BMP4.
source: Overexpression of Id4 in the absence of BMP induces many of the genes that BMP4 induces, and suppresses many of the genes suppressed by BMP4.
evidence: Summary of RNA-Seq comparison data

claim: Among the genes suppressed by both BMP4 treatment and Id4 overexpression, an important fraction corresponds to cell cycle regulators, including many Ascl1 targets.
source: Among the genes suppressed by both BMP4 treatment and Id4 overexpression, an important fraction corresponds to cell cycle regulators, including many Ascl1 targets.
evidence: Summary of RNA-Seq gene ontology analysis

claim: Id proteins promote a switch of the expression pattern of Hes proteins from oscillating to stably high, resulting in constant repression of target genes.
source: Therefore, Id proteins promote a switch of the expression pattern of Hes proteins from oscillating, resulting in oscillatory expression of target genes such as Ascl1, to stably high, resulting in constant repression of these targets (Bai et al., 2007; Boareto et al., 2017; Sueda et al., 2019).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies (Bai et al., 2007; Boareto et al., 2017; Sueda et al., 2019)

claim: Ascl1 is transcribed in most quiescent RGLs, indicating that Hes proteins do not repress Ascl1 transcription in these cells.
source: However, we find that Ascl1 is transcribed in most quiescent RGLs, indicating that Hes proteins do not repress Ascl1 transcription in these cells.
evidence: Inference based on the experimental finding that Ascl1 mRNA is present in quiescent RGLs

claim: Id4 has been shown to inhibit the action of Id1-3 proteins by interacting with stronger affinity with them than with other binding partners.
source: Id4 has been shown to inhibit the action of Id1-3 proteins by interacting with stronger affinity with them than with other binding partners (Patel et al., 2015; Sharma et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies (Patel et al., 2015; Sharma et al., 2015)

claim: Id4 promotes the proliferation of embryonic neural progenitors by blocking the interaction of Id1-3 with Hes proteins and thus promoting oscillations of Hes proteins and progenitor proliferation.
source: This non-canonical role of Id4 has been proposed to explain that Id4 promotes the proliferation of embryonic neural progenitors by blocking the interaction of Id1-3 with Hes proteins and thus promoting oscillations of Hes proteins – and consequently of Ascl1 – and progenitor proliferation (Bedford et al., 2005; Boareto et al., 2017; Yun et al., 2004).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies (Bedford et al., 2005; Boareto et al., 2017; Yun et al., 2004)

claim: Id4 deletion in RGLs in vivo results not only in upregulation of other Id proteins but also in a reduction of Ascl1 transcript levels.
source: In support of this model, Id4 deletion in RGLs in vivo results not only in upregulation of other Id proteins but also in a reduction of Ascl1 transcript levels.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from Id4cKO mice

claim: The function identified for Id4 in the hippocampus is distinct from the role reported for other Id factors in the adult V-SVZ, where Id1 and Id3 promote stem cell self-renewal.
source: The function that we have identified for Id4 in the hippocampus is also distinct from the role reported for other Id factors in the adult V-SVZ, where Id1 and Id3 promote stem cell self-renewal (Nam and Benezra, 2009) and Id1-3 maintain stem cell function by keeping stem cells adherent to their niche environment (Niola et al., 2012).
evidence: Comparison with previous studies cited (Nam and Benezra, 2009; Niola et al., 2012)

claim: Id4 expression is restricted to RGLs that are quiescent and express low levels or no Ascl1 protein.
source: While Id4 expression is restricted to RGLs that are quiescent and express low levels or no Ascl1 protein, Id1 protein is found in proliferating RGLs, many of which also express Ascl1 protein, suggesting that contrary to Id4, Id1 at the level it is expressed in RGLs in homeostasis does not promote stem cell quiescence or the degradation of Ascl1, although the same factor may have the potential to promote Ascl1 degradation when expressed at higher levels, that is when overexpressed in cultured NSCs.
evidence: Summary of immunofluorescence data comparing Id4 and Id1 expression patterns

claim: Id1 has been shown to have a role in the activation of hematopoietic stem cells upon stress signals.
source: In agreement with this, Id1 has recently been shown to have a role in the activation of hematopoietic stem cells upon stress signals (Singh et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement citing Singh et al., 2018

claim: Loss of Smad4 did not affect RGLs, indicating that Id1 is not required to suppress Ascl1 expression or RGL proliferation.
source: We have addressed the effect of loss of Id1 from RGLs by examining Smad4cKO mice, where Id1 expression in RGLs is greatly reduced while Id4 expression is unaffected (Blomfield et al., 2018). Loss of Smad4 did not affect RGLs, indicating that Id1 is not required to suppress Ascl1 expression or RGL proliferation.
evidence: Inference based on analysis of Smad4cKO mice, citing Blomfield et al., 2018

claim: Id3 expression is mostly restricted to quiescent RGLs and is therefore a better candidate to compensate for the loss of Id4 in quiescent cells.
source: Id3 expression, on the other hand, is mostly restricted to quiescent RGLs and is therefore a better candidate to compensate for the loss of Id4 in quiescent cells.
evidence: Inference based on Id3 expression pattern data

claim: Id4 deletion results in loss of quiescence of only a fraction of RGLs at both 5d and 30d post-deletion, suggesting that compensatory mechanisms operate to blunt the Id4cKO phenotype in RGLs.
source: While Id4 is expressed in the vast majority of quiescent RGLs, Id4 deletion results in loss of quiescence of only a fraction of them at both 5d and 30d post-deletion, suggesting that compensatory mechanisms operate to blunt the Id4cKO phenotype in RGLs.
evidence: Inference based on the incomplete penetrance of the Id4cKO phenotype

claim: Other Ids - in particular Id3 - or unrelated factors might compensate partially for the loss of Id4.
source: Thus, other Ids - in particular Id3, because of its expression pattern in quiescent RGLs - or unrelated factors might compensate partially for the loss of Id4.
evidence: Speculation based on the observed upregulation of Id3 in Id4cKO mice

claim: An increase in the repression of Ascl1 transcription, due to increased Hes-Id protein interactions and Hes protein stabilization, might contribute to the blunting of the Id4cKO phenotype.
source: An increase in the repression of Ascl1 transcription, due to increased Hes-Id protein interactions and Hes protein stabilization, might also contribute to the blunting of the Id4cKO phenotype.
evidence: Speculation based on known mechanisms of Hes-Id interactions

claim: Ascl1 transcription was lower in Id4cKO mice as early as 5 days after Id4 deletion.
source: In support of this, Ascl1 transcription was lower in Id4cKO mice as early as 5 days after Id4 deletion.
evidence: RNA in situ hybridization data from Id4cKO mice

claim: The ubiquitin ligase Huwe1 degrades Ascl1 in proliferating RGLs and allows a fraction of these cells to return to quiescence.
source: We have previously shown that the ubiquitin ligase Huwe1 degrades Ascl1 in proliferating RGLs and allows a fraction of these cells to return to quiescence (Urbán et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement citing previous study (Urbán et al., 2016)

claim: Huwe1 is expressed in quiescent RGLs.
source: Huwe1 is expressed in quiescent RGLs (Urbán et al., 2016) and although Id4 might mask its role in degrading Ascl1 in these cells, it might be able, in the absence of Id4, to eliminate excess Ascl1 and maintain RGL quiescence.
evidence: Statement citing previous study (Urbán et al., 2016)

claim: Id genes, including Id4, are well known effectors of BMP signalling in neural cells and other cell types.
source: Id genes, including Id4, are well known effectors of BMP signalling in neural cells and other cell types (Ling et al., 2014; Patel et al., 2015; Samanta and Kessler, 2004).
evidence: Statement of established knowledge with citations (Ling et al., 2014; Patel et al., 2015; Samanta and Kessler, 2004)

claim: Smad4 deletion strongly reduces Id1 but not Id4 levels in RGLs, indicating that Id4 diverges from other Id proteins in the regulation of its expression.
source: Smad4 deletion strongly reduces Id1 but not Id4 levels in RGLs, indicating that Id4 diverges from other Id proteins not only in its activity but also in the regulation of its expression (Blomfield et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement citing Blomfield et al., 2018

claim: Id4 has been shown to be directly regulated by Notch signalling in embryonic neural progenitors and in adult hippocampal stem cells.
source: Id4 has been shown to be directly regulated by Notch signalling in embryonic neural progenitors (Li et al., 2012) and in adult hippocampal stem cells (Zhang et al., 2019) but we found that Id4 expression persists in RGLs lacking the essential Notch signalling effector RBPJk (Blomfield et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies (Li et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2019; Blomfield et al., 2018)

claim: Id4 expression is only mildly affected in RGLs lacking both Smad4 and RBPJk, indicating that additional pathways beside BMP-Smad4 and Notch-Rbpjk promote RGL quiescence by maintaining Id4 expression.
source: Id4 expression is only mildly affected in RGLs lacking both Smad4 and RBPJk, indicating that additional pathways beside BMP-Smad4 and Notch-Rbpjk promote RGL quiescence by maintaining Id4 expression.
evidence: Inference based on analysis of double mutant mice, citing Blomfield et al., 2018

claim: Id4 is one of the most differentially expressed genes in quiescent versus active stem cells, both in vivo and in NSC cultures.
source: Indeed, it is one of the most differentially expressed genes in quiescent versus active stem cells, both in vivo and in NSC cultures (Shin et al., 2015 and this paper).
evidence: Statement citing previous study (Shin et al., 2015) and current study data

claim: Down-regulation of Id4 is crucial for RGLs to produce sufficient levels of Ascl1 protein to leave the quiescent state and become active.
source: Down-regulation of Id4 is crucial for RGLs to produce sufficient levels of Ascl1 protein to leave the quiescent state and become active, emphasizing the importance of this gene in the maintenance of RGL quiescence.
evidence: Inference based on the inverse relationship between Id4 and Ascl1 expression and the role of Ascl1 in activation

claim: Loss of Ascl1 completely blocks the activation of adult hippocampal stem cells, inhibits the generation of new neurons and prevents the depletion of the stem cell pool over time.
source: Loss of Ascl1 completely blocks the activation of adult hippocampal stem cells, inhibits the generation of new neurons and prevents the depletion of the stem cell pool over time (Andersen et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement citing Andersen et al., 2014

claim: Stabilization of Ascl1 protein by inactivation of the E3 ubiquitin ligase Huwe1 results in over-proliferation of hippocampal stem cells and prevents their return to quiescence.
source: Indeed, stabilization of Ascl1 protein by inactivation of the E3 ubiquitin ligase Huwe1 results in over-proliferation of hippocampal stem cells and prevents their return to quiescence (Urbán et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement citing Urbán et al., 2016

claim: Huwe1 inactivation is not sufficient to trigger the large-scale activation of quiescent stem cells.
source: However, Huwe1 inactivation is not sufficient to trigger the large-scale activation of quiescent stem cells, indicating that additional mechanisms maintain the quiescent state of hippocampal stem cells.
evidence: Statement citing Urbán et al., 2016 with inference about additional mechanisms

claim: Id proteins contain a conserved HLH domain with which they dimerize with some bHLH proteins but lack a DNA binding domain.
source: Id proteins contain a conserved HLH domain with which they dimerize with some bHLH proteins. However, they lack a DNA binding domain and therefore prevent bHLHs with which they interact from binding DNA and other bHLH factors (Benezra et al., 1990).
evidence: Statement of established knowledge citing Benezra et al., 1990

claim: Id proteins have been shown to sequester E proteins, the dimerization partners of Ascl1.
source: For instance, Id proteins have previously been shown to sequester E proteins, the dimerization partners of Ascl1.
evidence: Statement of established knowledge

claim: The resulting monomeric form of Ascl1 can no longer bind DNA and is furthermore rapidly degraded by the proteasome.
source: The resulting monomeric form of Ascl1 can no longer bind DNA and is furthermore rapidly degraded by the proteasome (Shou et al., 1999; Viñals et al., 2004).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies (Shou et al., 1999; Viñals et al., 2004)

claim: The Id genes are expressed in multiple tissues during development and in adult stem cell niches.
source: In mammals, the Id family comprises four genes, Id1-4. The Id genes are expressed in multiple tissues during development and in adult stem cell niches, and have been shown to promote stemness and proliferation in different systems, including in hematopoietic stem cells and in stem cells of the adult SVZ (Niola et al., 2012; Singh et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement of established knowledge with citations (Niola et al., 2012; Singh et al., 2018)

claim: Single cell transcriptome analysis has shown that expression of Id3 and Id4 in particular is highly enriched in quiescent hippocampal NSCs in vivo.
source: However single cell transcriptome analysis has also shown that expression of Id3 and Id4 in particular, is highly enriched in quiescent hippocampal NSCs in vivo, thus linking Id genes with NSC quiescence (Hochgerner et al., 2018; Shin et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement citing previous studies (Hochgerner et al., 2018; Shin et al., 2015)
